newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 22,750 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 45.519 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 22,500 tonnes and in Spain 250 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.419 million tonnes. This compares with the 27,900 tonnes awarded on February 7, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.588 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-July to be 45.518 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 30,000 and 60,000 tonnes versus 14,250 last week when the restitution was 45.422 Ecus.
